findings.title: Queued configuration cancellation is serialized before native dispatch
Batch cleanup rechecks external writers after taking HOME leases
Failed configuration calls revoke the captured admission certificate with CAS
Dependency rotation cannot redirect failure revocation to another scope
Preflight rejection preserves a newer admission certificate
Concurrent configuration completion returns one coherent payload snapshot
Native history changes before batch lease abort cleanup without side effects
Physical native spawn survives journal failure with conservative certificate revocation
Version-named, renamed, interpreter and opaque native writers are handled conservatively
SQLite journal faults finalize configuration and revoke started-call admission
Post-Popen worker or terminal metadata failure leaves an owned child live and untracked

limitations: The frozen 203-file candidate identity matches the supplied candidate hash and tree identity; source was not modified. The focused current 87-case configuration suite, 44 agent-session tests, 98 admission/provenance/UX tests, and all-candidate Python AST parsing passed locally.

Independent scratch-only harmless-child probes injected metadata publication failure after successful Popen. They observed a live child before reviewer cleanup for ConfigurationAssistant.start at tools/studio/configuration_assistant.py:124-126, NativeTerminals.start at tools/studio/native_terminals.py:107-119, WorkbenchRuntime.spawn at tools/studio/workbench_runtime.py:321-327, and SessionCenter.launch at tools/studio/session_center.py:311-315. The configuration SQLite-error path also escaped with the operation still QUEUED; OSError paths commonly marked FAILED but still retained the live child. The probe did not invoke a provider or read credentials.

The inner orchestration.process post-Popen journal boundary is independently closed: current focused tests and sealed SQLite evidence show process_started retention, group kill/reap, pipe closure, finalization, captured-record CAS, and pre-spawn cancellation preservation. That evidence does not cover the separate detached-supervisor and PTY-terminal Popen-to-metadata windows identified here.

The current 87-case run and sealed normal-host 21-test supplement passed. One local outer-bwrap isolation test could not run because this reviewer kernel disallows unprivileged user namespaces; the current external normal-host record passed that suite. Broad 737-Python/Chromium/JS/build/privacy and real native journeys were inspected from sealed evidence rather than fully replayed locally.

The current native Codex/Claude and configuration journeys support the recorded same-UUID and proposal claims, but physical backend identity and effective effort remain unknown; user personal UX acceptance remains pending. The old fixed Gate refusal remains historical and no new Gate, merge, Stable promotion, authority write, authentication read, or external publication was performed.

The new P1 is sufficient for NEEDS_CORRECTION rather than BLOCKED: it is directly reproducible with a harmless local child and source inspection. Repair must make every relevant post-Popen ownership publication failure kill/reap the exact process group and durably finalize or conservatively mark the operation, while retaining pre-spawn no-child behavior and existing captured-record/CAS guarantees.
